A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe IPFormer and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A. Pages 2–19 are textually and visually identical; differences are confined to the first page.

before.justification: v2 reports original IPFormer evaluations on SemanticKITTI and SSCBench-KITTI360, ablation experiments, qualitative results, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative evaluations, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same context-adaptive proposal initialization, attention architecture, dual heads, two-stage training, losses, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use SemanticKITTI for in-domain experiments and SSCBench-KITTI360 for zero-shot evaluation. Dataset, task, and scenario coverage are unchanged throughout the main text and appendix.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MonoScene, Symphonies, OccFormer, and CGFormer, each combined with DBSCAN. Table 2 retains CGFormer+DBSCAN, and appendix comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The data splits, preprocessing, metrics, training settings, checkpoint selection, and clustering protocol in Sections 4.1 and A.1–A.2 are identical. Table 9 retains the same 20% versus 50% IoU matching-threshold evaluation.

E4.justification: Tables 3–6 and 9–10 retain the same initialization, visibility, deep-supervision, architecture, training, matching-threshold, and loss-hyperparameter studies. Saliency analyses and qualitative examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting without repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–10 and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports IPFormer PQ-All of 6.30 and runtime of 0.33 seconds in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(12), including proposal construction, attention operations, training losses, and panoptic metric definitions, are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about context-adaptive instance proposals, state-of-the-art in-domain performance, zero-shot generalization, and runtime reduction exceeding 14 times.

C2.justification: Interpretations of proposal adaptivity and SSC/PSC tradeoffs are unchanged. Appendix A.6 retains the same limitations concerning unrecognized classes and the inability to compare directly with PanoSSC.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and clustering instructions are identical. The existing repository link moves from beneath the affiliations to the abstract, with the same destination and no substantive access-information change.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged, including positioning relative to Symphonies, CGFormer, and PanoSSC. No cited works or substantive research-positioning statements are added or removed.

P1.justification: The first page updates affiliation assignments, adds Munich Center for Machine Learning and UCLA affiliations, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The relocated repository link gains 'Code available at' wording; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block and relocation of the code link into the abstract cause localized first-page reflow. Figures 1–5, Tables 1–10, and the layout of pages 2–19 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 updates affiliations and rearranges the existing code disclosure, but preserves all scientific content, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility details, including the appendix. These localized front-matter edits establish no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
